headline: India Slashes Cancer Drug Costs After Court Rules Markups 'Extortion'
meta_description: India's court intervention has forced a dramatic reduction in cancer medication prices, deeming excessive markups a form of extortion.
summary_short: Following a court ruling that branded excessive markups as 'extortion,' India has significantly reduced the cost of cancer drugs, bringing relief to patients.
body:
India has slashed the cost of cancer drugs after a court ruled that steep markups on these life-saving medications constituted extortion. The legal intervention marks a turning point in the country's struggle to make essential treatments affordable for patients facing one of the world's deadliest diseases.

The court's decision reframes what many have long suspected: that pricing cancer medications far beyond production costs exploits vulnerable patients in their most desperate moments. By categorizing extreme markups as extortion rather than standard business practice, the ruling creates legal precedent for challenging pharmaceutical pricing across the board.

This development offers hope to India's millions of cancer patients, many of whom have historically faced impossible choices between treatment and financial ruin. The price cuts demonstrate that judicial intervention can work alongside regulatory reform to protect public health when market forces alone fail.
quick_facts: India's court ruled that drug markups on cancer treatments constitute 'extortion'
Cancer drug prices have been significantly reduced following the ruling
The decision affects millions of Indian patients facing treatment costs
